items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (Condition 7010d0e5) and no anticoagulant at any time in the chart: current medications are tamsulosin/levothyroxine only (cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27), and no oral anticoagulant order exists. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease = coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at score >=2 in men. Needs review for initiation (history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 2026-03-02 cardiology clinic visit; it first appears on that visit's medication list and the order was authored the same day. Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07 (day 5) and reported in the 2026-03-07 clinic note; QTc ~366 ms. Requirement met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit (first amiodarone outpatient order 5d345f42 authored that day; it is absent from the 2025-09-21 visit list and present from 2025-11-10). Start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24 (day 14). Requirement met, but that tracing shows QTc ~553 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-02-12 cardiology clinic visit (first order 0d807827 authored that day). Because the start preceded 3/1/2026 the earlier memo's 30-day window is retained, so the ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08 (day 24) - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - with sinus rhythm at 68 bpm and QTc ~450 ms. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-04-10 cardiology clinic visit (first order ead8699a authored that day). Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met in time and is now overdue (it would have been met under the superseded 30-day memo). Escitalopram remains current (order b9bce5cd to 2027-01-01).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-08-01 cardiology clinic visit (order 9fa1dfe1, valid to 2026-12-26, and newly listed on that visit's medication list). An ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and none is referenced elsewhere, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-08-10 cardiology clinic visit (order d7292a2a), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The 2026-08-25 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG for this patient exists in the chart. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-09-15 cardiology clinic visit (order 34d26a30, valid to 2027-01-06; first appearance on the medication list). Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due; an ECG should be arranged this month.

At the 2026-09-01 cardiology clinic visit the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the 3/1/2026 memo covers, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the change and no pending outside result is referenced, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 (Condition 66dd1300) during an admission for cerebral infarction. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered: cardiology clinic notes 2025-04-24 through 2026-06-23 list only famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine, and the only heparin exposure was a single inpatient prophylaxis dose in 3/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Documented thrombocytopenia and history of falling should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit, despite outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug was restarted/continued without that review being documented; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was re-issued the same day and the note's own medication list includes both agents. Rivaroxaban must be stopped; combined DOAC therapy carries a major haemorrhage risk in a patient also on clopidogrel.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', but both ECGs recorded that day contradict it: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.36-0.53 s) with no organised P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong, and the patient carries an unspecified-atrial-fibrillation diagnosis; rate control and the accuracy of the record need review.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 438668cc, 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuous since 5/2024). Most recent ECG 108018814 (2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~495 ms and Bazett QTc ~529 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL on 2026-03-18). Note the 2024-05-14 clinic note characterised this tracing's QT as 'acceptable', which the measured QTc does not support; a repeat ECG is also reasonable given the tracing is nearly three years old.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order e78404bf, 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG 106885519 (2025-11-24) is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a broad low-amplitude T wave, QT ~545 ms and Bazett QTc ~553 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo; QTc rose ~143 ms from the prior tracing (410 ms on 2025-06-07). Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Concurrent warfarin interaction and torsades risk warrant prescriber review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 62da0901, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; continuous since 10/2023) - a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised where QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent ECG 104821039 (2023-11-10) is sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~480 ms and Bazett QTc ~533 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, and ~147 ms longer than the prior tracing (386 ms, 2020-06-17). Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. Prescriber review of dose/agent and a current ECG are needed.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order c67148bf, 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06; continuous since 2022). Most recent ECG 101515306 (2022-04-27) is sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a very broad T wave, QT ~580 ms and Bazett QTc ~568 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo and ~128 ms longer than the prior tracing (440 ms, 2022-04-06). Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are acceptable though magnesium is at the low end. This 95-year-old is also on warfarin and metoprolol; prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.

interpretations.explanation: ECG 104882441 (2026-03-07): regular narrow-complex rhythm at 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave in II/aVF preceding every QRS (P-P matches R-R), i.e. normal sinus rhythm; mild rate drift (RR 0.66-0.86 s) is sinus arrhythmia, and PR-segment depression follows the P. PR ~185 ms, QRS ~86 ms, QT ~316 ms giving Bazett QTc ~366 ms at RR 0.74 s. Net QRS forces positive in I and aVF (frontal axis ~+48 degrees, normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. The tracing confirms the same-day note's 'sinus rhythm' and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

ECG 108195884 (2025-07-15): regular rhythm at 104 bpm (RR 0.58 s, CV 0.009) with a discrete upright P wave in I/II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~150 ms, QRS ~98 ms with deep S in V2; QT ~348 ms, Bazett QTc ~457 ms (mildly prolonged). Frontal axis ~+39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147 bpm with T-P fusion; measuring the T offset before the P hump gives QT ~280 ms and QTc ~440 ms, so the change in QTc is under 60 ms and the rhythm was also supraventricular/sinus - no changes are reported.

ECG 105862861 (2024-05-21): regular rhythm at 110 bpm with upright P waves in II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~125 ms, QRS ~92 ms, QT ~318 ms, Bazett QTc ~430 ms. Frontal axis ~+36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG in the chart, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be assessed.

ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36): irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean of 144 bpm (RR 0.36-0.53 s, CV 0.16) with no reproducible P wave before the QRS (pre-QRS correlation 0.49) and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS ~102 ms, QT ~280 ms, Bazett QTc ~434 ms. Frontal axis ~-2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 h 20 min earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QTc ~432 ms, so there are no changes. Both tracings contradict the same-day clinic note documenting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which is raised as a separate contradiction item.

ECG 103992480 (2025-08-02): regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR CV 0.006) with a small atrial deflection before each QRS, best seen as a positive wave in lead I with a shallow negative component in II (leftward P axis); PR ~145 ms. QRS ~86 ms, QT ~408 ms, Bazett QTc ~437 ms. Frontal axis ~-25 degrees (within the normal -30 to +90 range). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, regular 60 bpm, QRS ~86 ms, QTc ~405 ms) the QTc is ~32 ms longer, below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are listed.

ECG 107627609 (2024-05-23): regular rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS - sinus rhythm. PR ~125 ms, QRS ~78 ms, QT ~298 ms, Bazett QTc ~380 ms. Frontal axis ~+5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing and no changes to report.

ECG 106035722 (2025-12-25): regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS; PR ~135 ms, QRS ~88 ms, QT ~368 ms, Bazett QTc ~403 ms - within normal limits and well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Frontal axis ~+22 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. It predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram and therefore does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement, which is raised separately.

ECG 108912996 (2024-11-15): irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.70-1.16 s, CV 0.20) with no consistent P wave - the pre-QRS segment correlates poorly across beats (0.20) and the baseline shows coarse fibrillatory activity - atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean rate ~53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS ~96 ms, QT ~448 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms. Frontal axis ~+27 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107873952 (2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR ~185 ms) and QTc ~386 ms, so NEW_AF is reported; the QTc change (~35 ms) is below threshold. Apixaban is already prescribed.

ECG 104253928 (2025-03-09): regular rhythm at 58 bpm with a prominent upright P wave in II before each QRS - sinus bradycardia. PR ~115 ms, QRS ~90 ms, QT ~426 ms, Bazett QTc ~420 ms. Frontal axis ~+60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 106045460 from the previous day (sinus 62 bpm, QRS ~90 ms, QTc ~436 ms) there is no meaningful change (QTc ~16 ms shorter). Both tracings long predate the 2026-09-15 start of haloperidol, so a new ECG is required under the QT memo.

ECG 106565956 (2025-08-23): regular sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (RR CV 0.004) with an upright P in II preceding each QRS; PR ~145 ms, QRS ~76 ms, QT ~344 ms, Bazett QTc ~405 ms. Frontal axis ~+54 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be determined.

ECG 109952008 (2020-06-19): regular sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a tall upright P in II (PR ~158 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~74 ms, QT ~384 ms, Bazett QTc ~434 ms. Frontal axis ~+65 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus 75 bpm, QRS ~68 ms, QT ~500 ms, QTc ~555 ms) the QTc has shortened by ~120 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is reported; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

ECG 105523266 (2021-01-18): very regular rhythm at 121 bpm (RR 0.49-0.50 s, CV 0.005) with an upright P wave in I/II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~200 ms (upper limit of normal, not exceeding it), QRS ~88 ms, QT ~248 ms and Bazett QTc ~351 ms. Frontal axis ~+56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 107 bpm, QRS ~106 ms, QTc ~393 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc is ~41 ms shorter, below the 60 ms reporting threshold, so no changes are listed.

ECG 102280728 (2025-06-23): regular rhythm at 54 bpm with a broad upright P wave in II beginning about 215 ms before QRS onset and conducting 1:1 - sinus bradycardia with a prolonged PR interval of ~213 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS ~86 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~400 ms, Bazett QTc ~381 ms. Frontal axis ~+1 degree (normal). Versus the prior tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51 bpm, PR ~190 ms, QRS ~88 ms, QTc ~364 ms) the QTc change is only ~17 ms and the rhythm is unchanged, so no changes are listed (PR prolongation is not one of the reportable change categories).

ECG 108211642 (2025-09-13): chaotically irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean of 153 bpm (RR 0.29-0.58 s, CV 0.19) with a flat lead II baseline and no identifiable P waves (pre-QRS correlation 0.15) - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS ~96 ms, QT ~256 ms, Bazett QTc ~408 ms. Frontal axis ~-11 to -20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107374881 (2025-09-12) was a regular rhythm at 77 bpm with P waves and QTc ~419 ms, so NEW_AF is reported; the QTc difference (~11 ms) is not significant. Apixaban is already current.

ECG 102172660 (2025-11-23): regular sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a clear upright P wave in II (PR ~172 ms) before each QRS, matching the same-day clinic note's 'ECG today: sinus rhythm'. QRS ~94 ms, QT ~342 ms, Bazett QTc ~378 ms. Frontal axis ~+11 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67 bpm, QRS ~90 ms, QT ~495 ms, QTc ~525 ms) the QTc has shortened by ~147 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is reported. The patient takes no QT watch-list drug.

ECG 106825293 (2025-02-15): regular sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS; PR ~165 ms, QRS ~92 ms, QT ~374 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Frontal axis ~+58 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be assessed.

ECG 102853474 (2023-06-26): metronomically regular rhythm at 112 bpm (RR 0.538 s, CV 0.003) with an upright P wave in II peaking ~110 ms before QRS onset - sinus tachycardia. PR ~165 ms, QRS ~98 ms with a deep S in V1 (-3.0 mV) and tall positive T waves in V1-V2. QT ~276 ms, Bazett QTc ~376 ms. Frontal axis ~+35 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS ~96 ms, QTc ~356 ms) nothing has changed beyond a 20 ms QTc difference. Note the chart records atrial flutter diagnoses, but neither tracing shows flutter.

ECG 102298909 (2025-03-14): baseline rhythm regular at 61 bpm with an upright P wave in I and II before each conducted beat (PR ~190-195 ms, at the upper limit but not exceeding 200 ms); one early beat with a compensatory pause accounts for the RR scatter (0.98, 0.98, 0.54, 1.37, 0.98 s), i.e. sinus rhythm with a single premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. QRS ~104 ms, QT ~358 ms, Bazett QTc ~362 ms. Frontal axis ~-22 to -30 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was nevertheless documented on this admission and she is not anticoagulated, which is raised separately.

ECG 107859369 (2026-04-29): regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.84-0.88 s) with a reproducible atrial deflection before every QRS (PR ~120 ms) - sinus rhythm. QRS ~94 ms, QT ~356 ms, Bazett QTc ~383 ms. The frontal plane is unusual: QRS is almost entirely negative in lead I (S -1.4 mV) with a tall R in aVR and a near-isoelectric aVF, giving a computed frontal axis of about -172 to -175 degrees, which falls in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; the P wave is also negative in I and II and positive in aVR while precordial R-wave progression is entirely normal, a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

ECG 104821039 (2023-11-10): regular sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~155 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~104 ms. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~480-495 ms, Bazett QTc ~530 ms at RR 0.86 s - clearly prolonged. Frontal axis ~+41 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS ~82 ms, QTc ~386 ms) the QTc has increased by ~145 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is reported. The patient has taken citalopram 40 mg daily since 10/2023, and this tracing drives a QT safety review item.

ECG 101538691 (2026-03-08): regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~145 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~90 ms. There is deep symmetric T-wave inversion in I, aVL, V2 and V5-V6 with reciprocal tall T in III/aVR; taking the latest T offset across leads gives QT ~420-435 ms and Bazett QTc ~450-465 ms (reported 455 ms) - mildly prolonged but below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Frontal axis ~+61 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. It was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and satisfies the applicable 30-day monitoring window; the widespread T inversion in a patient with known coronary disease deserves clinical correlation.

ECG 107689861 (2019-01-13): regular rhythm at 53 bpm with an upright P wave in II beginning ~180 ms before QRS onset - sinus bradycardia with a normal PR interval. QRS ~94 ms, QT ~378 ms, Bazett QTc ~355 ms. Frontal axis ~-3 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, QRS ~106 ms, QTc ~387 ms) the QTc is ~32 ms shorter, below the reporting threshold, and the rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG 108018814 (2023-10-08): regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P in II (biphasic in V1) before every QRS. PR ~158 ms, QRS ~94 ms. The T wave is broad and late-peaking: QT ~495 ms, Bazett QTc ~529 ms at RR 0.88 s - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis ~+44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QTc ~348 ms) the QTc has lengthened by ~180 ms, hence QTC_INCREASE_60; the patient has been on escitalopram since 5/2024, and this prolongation is the basis of a QT safety review item.

ECG 100924231 (2022-07-13): regular narrow-complex rhythm at 141 bpm (RR 0.40-0.45 s, CV 0.02) with a reproducible atrial deflection ~130-175 ms before each QRS and an isoelectric segment between atrial and ventricular activity, consistent with sinus tachycardia rather than a flutter sawtooth; PR ~175 ms. QRS ~84 ms, QT ~264 ms, Bazett QTc ~405 ms. Frontal axis ~0 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block and no pacing spikes despite the recorded pacemaker. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed an irregularly irregular rhythm (RR 0.38-0.82 s, CV 0.24) with no organised atrial activity, i.e. atrial fibrillation, so RESOLVED_AF is reported; QTc changed by only ~18 ms. Given the rate and the flutter history, 2:1 atrial flutter cannot be excluded with complete certainty.

ECG 102888469 (2025-05-12): regular sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~158 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~104 ms - a mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay but below the 120 ms needed for bundle branch block. QT ~376 ms, Bazett QTc ~441 ms. Frontal axis ~+34 degrees (normal); no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be assessed.

ECG 103036945 (2022-07-16): regular sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~175 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~84 ms, QT ~300 ms, Bazett QTc ~369 ms. Frontal axis ~-12 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus 87 bpm, QRS ~86 ms, QTc ~335 ms) the QTc is ~34 ms longer, below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are reported.

ECG 104941853 (2024-07-17): underlying rhythm regular at 61 bpm (RR 0.95-1.00 s; one long interval at the start of the recording reflects signal dropout) with an upright P wave in II starting ~210 ms before QRS onset - sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block (PR ~208 ms). QRS is broad at ~132 ms with a QS complex in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 and absent septal q waves - complete left bundle branch block. QT ~434 ms, Bazett QTc ~438 ms. Frontal axis ~-21 to -25 degrees (normal). Versus the prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) the findings are essentially identical (sinus ~68 bpm, QRS 132 ms with the same left bundle branch block, QTc ~431 ms), so there is no new or resolved bundle branch block and no significant QTc change.

ECG 107457843 (2025-03-19): regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~150 ms) before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. QRS ~92 ms, QT ~326 ms, Bazett QTc ~424 ms. Frontal axis ~+46 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 101016166 from the previous day (sinus 102 bpm, QRS ~90 ms, QTc ~419 ms) the tracings are essentially identical, so no changes are reported.

ECG 109419304 (2025-09-22): regular sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with an upright P wave in II (PR ~165 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~92 ms, QT ~366 ms, Bazett QTc ~383 ms. Frontal axis ~-20 to -26 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be determined.

ECG 101515306 (2022-04-27): regular rhythm at 58 bpm (RR 0.97-1.10 s) with a low upright P wave in II beginning ~195 ms before QRS onset and conducting 1:1 - sinus bradycardia with a PR at the upper limit of normal. QRS ~92 ms. The T wave is extremely broad and late-peaking: QT ~575-580 ms, Bazett QTc ~568 ms - grossly prolonged, consistent with chronic amiodarone. Frontal axis ~+38 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior tracing 100867733 (2022-04-06) was atrial fibrillation with a rapid, chaotically irregular ventricular response (mean 131 bpm, RR 0.32-1.06 s, CV 0.33) and QTc ~440 ms, so RESOLVED_AF and QTC_INCREASE_60 (+128 ms) are both reported. The prolonged QTc drives a separate QT safety item.

ECG 101524902 (2022-05-01): regular rhythm at 107 bpm with an upright P wave in II (PR ~150 ms) before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. QRS ~70 ms, QT ~302 ms, Bazett QTc ~404 ms. Frontal axis ~+53 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. Versus the prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, QRS ~76 ms, QTc ~422 ms) the QTc is ~18 ms shorter, below the reporting threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

ECG 109218019 (2024-04-19): regular rhythm at 121 bpm, RR 0.49-0.50 s with negligible variation, and a discrete upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~140 ms, QRS ~78 ms, QT ~256 ms, Bazett QTc ~363 ms. Frontal axis ~+71 degrees (normal, vertical). No bundle branch block, no AV block. This is the only ECG for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

ECG 109661561 (2021-08-23 10:07): regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR ~160 ms) before each of 16 beats. QRS ~92 ms with an rS in V1 and tall R in V6; QT ~316 ms, Bazett QTc ~411 ms. Frontal axis ~+58 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, QRS ~94 ms, QTc ~406 ms), so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

ECG 107158938 (2024-10-24): regular rhythm at 52 bpm (RR 1.15-1.18 s) with a low broad upright P wave in II before each QRS - sinus bradycardia. interpretations.explanation: ECG 104882441 (2026-03-07): regular narrow-complex rhythm at 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave in II/aVF preceding every QRS (P-P matches R-R), i.e. normal sinus rhythm; mild rate drift (RR 0.66-0.86 s) is sinus arrhythmia, and PR-segment depression follows the P. PR ~185 ms, QRS ~86 ms, QT ~316 ms giving Bazett QTc ~366 ms at RR 0.74 s. Net QRS forces positive in I and aVF (frontal axis ~+48 degrees, normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. The tracing confirms the same-day note's 'sinus rhythm' and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

ECG 105523266 (2021-01-18): very regular rhythm at 121 bpm (RR 0.49-0.50 s, CV 0.005) with an upright P wave in I/II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~200 ms (upper limit of normal, not exceeding it), QRS ~88 ms, QT ~248 ms and Bazett QTc ~351 ms. Frontal axis ~+56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 107 bpm, QRS ~106 ms, QTc ~393 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc is ~41 ms shorter, below the 60 ms reporting threshold, so no changes are listed.

ECG 108018814 (2023-10-08): regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P in II (biphasic in V1) before every QRS. PR ~158 ms, QRS ~94 ms. The T wave is broad and late-peaking: QT ~495 ms, Bazett QTc ~529 ms at RR 0.88 s - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis ~+44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QTc ~348 ms) the QTc has lengthened by ~180 ms, hence QTC_INCREASE_60; the patient has been on escitalopram since 5/2024, and this prolongation is the basis of a QT safety review item.

This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. The tracing confirms the same-day note's 'sinus rhythm' and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

ECG 108195884 (2025-07-15): regular rhythm at 104 bpm (RR 0.58 s, CV 0.009) with a discrete upright P wave in I/II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~150 ms, QRS ~98 ms with deep S in V2; QT ~348 ms, Bazett QTc ~457 ms (mildly prolonged). Frontal axis ~+39 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) was a regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 147 bpm with T-P fusion; measuring the T offset before the P hump gives QT ~280 ms and QTc ~440 ms, so the change in QTc is under 60 ms and the rhythm was also supraventricular/sinus - no changes are reported.

ECG 105862861 (2024-05-21): regular rhythm at 110 bpm with upright P waves in II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~125 ms, QRS ~92 ms, QT ~318 ms, Bazett QTc ~430 ms. Frontal axis ~+36 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG in the chart, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be assessed.

ECG 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36): irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at a mean of 144 bpm (RR 0.36-0.53 s, CV 0.16) with no reproducible P wave before the QRS (pre-QRS correlation 0.49) and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS ~102 ms, QT ~280 ms, Bazett QTc ~434 ms. Frontal axis ~-2 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107914094, recorded 2 h 20 min earlier the same day, shows the same atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QTc ~432 ms, so there are no changes. Both tracings contradict the same-day clinic note documenting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which is raised as a separate contradiction item.

ECG 103992480 (2025-08-02): regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR CV 0.006) with a small atrial deflection before each QRS, best seen as a positive wave in lead I with a shallow negative component in II (leftward P axis); PR ~145 ms. QRS ~86 ms, QT ~408 ms, Bazett QTc ~437 ms. Frontal axis ~-25 degrees (within the normal -30 to +90 range). No bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27, regular 60 bpm, QRS ~86 ms, QTc ~405 ms) the QTc is ~32 ms longer, below the 60 ms threshold, so no changes are listed.

ECG 107627609 (2024-05-23): regular rhythm at 97 bpm with an upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS - sinus rhythm. PR ~125 ms, QRS ~78 ms, QT ~298 ms, Bazett QTc ~380 ms. Frontal axis ~+5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so there is no prior tracing and no changes to report.

ECG 106035722 (2025-12-25): regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS; PR ~135 ms, QRS ~88 ms, QT ~368 ms, Bazett QTc ~403 ms - within normal limits and well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Frontal axis ~+22 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. It predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram and therefore does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement, which is raised separately.

ECG 108912996 (2024-11-15): irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.70-1.16 s, CV 0.20) with no consistent P wave - the pre-QRS segment correlates poorly across beats (0.20) and the baseline shows coarse fibrillatory activity - atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean rate ~53 bpm. No measurable PR interval. QRS ~96 ms, QT ~448 ms, Bazett QTc ~421 ms. Frontal axis ~+27 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107873952 (2024-11-12) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR ~185 ms) and QTc ~386 ms, so NEW_AF is reported; the QTc change (~35 ms) is below threshold. Apixaban is already prescribed.

ECG 104253928 (2025-03-09): regular rhythm at 58 bpm with a prominent upright P wave in II before each QRS - sinus bradycardia. PR ~115 ms, QRS ~90 ms, QT ~426 ms, Bazett QTc ~420 ms. Frontal axis ~+60 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 106045460 from the previous day (sinus 62 bpm, QRS ~90 ms, QTc ~436 ms) there is no meaningful change (QTc ~16 ms shorter). Both tracings long predate the 2026-09-15 start of haloperidol, so a new ECG is required under the QT memo.

Frontal axis ~+65 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus 75 bpm, QRS ~68 ms, QT ~500 ms, QTc ~555 ms) the QTc has shortened by ~120 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is reported; rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

PR ~200 ms (upper limit of normal, not exceeding it), QRS ~88 ms, QT ~248 ms and Bazett QTc ~351 ms. Frontal axis ~+56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 107 bpm, QRS ~106 ms, QTc ~393 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc is ~41 ms shorter, below the 60 ms reporting threshold, so no changes are listed.

QRS ~86 ms (no bundle branch block), QT ~400 ms, Bazett QTc ~381 ms. Frontal axis ~+1 degree (normal). Versus the prior tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51 bpm, PR ~190 ms, QRS ~88 ms, QTc ~364 ms) the QTc change is only ~17 ms and the rhythm is unchanged, so no changes are listed (PR prolongation is not one of the reportable change categories).

No measurable PR interval. QRS ~96 ms, QT ~256 ms, Bazett QTc ~408 ms. Frontal axis ~-11 to -20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior tracing 107374881 (2025-09-12) was a regular rhythm at 77 bpm with P waves and QTc ~419 ms, so NEW_AF is reported; the QTc difference (~11 ms) is not significant. Apixaban is already current.

Versus the prior tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus 67 bpm, QRS ~90 ms, QT ~495 ms, QTc ~525 ms) the QTc has shortened by ~147 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is reported. The patient takes no QT watch-list drug.

ECG 106825293 (2025-02-15): regular sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS; PR ~165 ms, QRS ~92 ms, QT ~374 ms, Bazett QTc ~416 ms. Frontal axis ~+58 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so prior_ecg is null and no changes can be assessed.

ECG 102853474 (2023-06-26): metronomically regular rhythm at 112 bpm (RR 0.538 s, CV 0.003) with an upright P wave in II peaking ~110 ms before QRS onset - sinus tachycardia. PR ~165 ms, QRS ~98 ms with a deep S in V1 (-3.0 mV) and tall positive T waves in V1-V2. QT ~276 ms, Bazett QTc ~376 ms. Frontal axis ~+35 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS ~96 ms, QTc ~356 ms) nothing has changed beyond a 20 ms QTc difference. Note the chart records atrial flutter diagnoses, but neither tracing shows flutter.

ECG 102298909 (2025-03-14): baseline rhythm regular at 61 bpm with an upright P wave in I and II before each conducted beat (PR ~190-195 ms, at the upper limit but not exceeding 200 ms); one early beat with a compensatory pause accounts for the RR scatter (0.98, 0.98, 0.54, 1.37, 0.98 s), i.e. sinus rhythm with a single premature complex rather than atrial fibrillation. QRS ~104 ms, QT ~358 ms, Bazett QTc ~362 ms. Frontal axis ~-22 to -30 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was nevertheless documented on this admission and she is not anticoagulated, which is raised separately.

ECG 107859369 (2026-04-29): regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.84-0.88 s) with a reproducible atrial deflection before every QRS (PR ~120 ms) - sinus rhythm. QRS ~94 ms, QT ~356 ms, Bazett QTc ~383 ms. The frontal plane is unusual: QRS is almost entirely negative in lead I (S -1.4 mV) with a tall R in aVR and a near-isoelectric aVF, giving a computed frontal axis of about -172 to -175 degrees, which falls in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; the P wave is also negative in I and II and positive in aVR while precordial R-wave progression is entirely normal, a pattern that strongly suggests left/right arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation - the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG for this patient, so no prior comparison.

ECG 104821039 (2023-11-10): regular sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~155 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~104 ms. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~480-495 ms, Bazett QTc ~530 ms at RR 0.86 s - clearly prolonged. Frontal axis ~+41 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS ~82 ms, QTc ~386 ms) the QTc has increased by ~145 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is reported. The patient has taken citalopram 40 mg daily since 10/2023, and this tracing drives a QT safety review item.

ECG 108018814 (2023-10-08): regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P in II (biphasic in V1) before every QRS. PR ~158 ms, QRS ~94 ms. The T wave is broad and late-peaking: QT ~495 ms, Bazett QTc ~529 ms at RR 0.88 s - markedly prolonged. Frontal axis ~+44 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QTc ~348 ms) the QTc has lengthened by ~180 ms, hence QTC_INCREASE_60; the patient has been on escitalopram since 5/2024, and this prolongation is the basis of a QT safety review item.

This is the only ECG for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

ECG 109661561 (2021-08-23 10:07): regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF (PR ~160 ms) before each of 16 beats. QRS ~92 ms with an rS in V1 and tall R in V6; QT ~316 ms, Bazett QTc ~411 ms. Frontal axis ~+58 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, QRS ~94 ms, QTc ~406 ms), so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

ECG 107158938 (2024-10-24): regular rhythm at 52 bpm (RR 1.15-1.18 s) with a low broad upright P wave in II before each QRS - sinus bradycardia. PR ~172 ms, QRS ~94 ms, QT ~430 ms, Bazett QTc ~401 ms. Voltages are large (R 1.2 mV in I, 3.3 mV in V6) suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy, but the axis is normal at ~+37 degrees and there is no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus 58 bpm with a single premature beat, QRS ~90 ms, QTc ~388 ms) nothing has changed beyond a slower rate.

ECG 101901982 (2024-12-05 14:38): regular rhythm at 122 bpm (RR 0.49 s, CV 0.002) with an upright P in II before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. PR ~150 ms, QRS now narrow at ~74 ms, QT ~258 ms, Bazett QTc ~367 ms. Net QRS is negative in I and slightly positive in aVF, giving a frontal axis of about +135 to +157 degrees - right axis deviation. Compared with the prior tracing 106516875 from 01:33 the same day (QRS 158 ms with a broad tall R in V1 and wide S in I - complete right bundle branch block - and QTc ~452 ms), the right bundle branch block has resolved and the QTc has fallen by ~85 ms, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK and QTC_DECREASE_60 are reported.

ECG 106885519 (2025-11-24): regular sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a low broad upright P wave in II preceding every QRS; PR ~170 ms, QRS ~100 ms. The T wave is very broad and low amplitude with a late return to baseline: QT ~545 ms, Bazett QTc ~553 ms at RR 0.97 s - markedly prolonged, the typical amiodarone pattern. Frontal axis ~+67 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. Versus the prior tracing 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QRS ~102 ms, QTc ~410 ms) the QTc has increased by ~143 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is reported; this underlies the QT safety review item.

ECG 109287357 (2024-09-17): grossly irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS segments are inconsistent from beat to beat (mean cross-correlation 0.45) and only fibrillatory baseline undulation is seen - i.e. atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate ~99 bpm. No measurable PR interval, so pr_ms is null. QRS ~84 ms, QT ~318 ms, Bazett QTc ~409 ms (using median RR 0.61 s). Net QRS negative in aVF and positive in I gives a frontal axis of about -45 to -52 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. No bundle branch block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible; it corroborates the atrial fibrillation diagnosis for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

arguments.explanation: ECG 101538691 (2026-03-08): regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with an upright P in II (PR ~145 ms) before each QRS. QRS ~90 ms. There is deep symmetric T-wave inversion in I, aVL, V2 and V5-V6 with reciprocal tall T in III/aVR; taking the latest T offset across leads gives QT ~420-435 ms and Bazett QTc ~450-465 ms (reported 455 ms) - mildly prolonged but below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Frontal axis ~+61 degrees (normal); no bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible. It was obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started and satisfies the applicable 30-day monitoring window; the widespread T inversion in a patient with known coronary disease deserves clinical correlation.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (Condition 7010d0e5) and no anticoagulant at any time in the chart: current medications are tamsulosin/levothyroxine only (cardiology clinic notes 2025-10-10 through 2026-06-27), and no oral anticoagulant order exists. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease = coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation at score >=2 in men. Needs review for initiation (history of hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 2026-03-02 cardiology clinic visit; it first appears on that visit's medication list and the order was authored the same day. Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07 (day 5) and reported in the 2026-03-07 clinic note; QTc ~366 ms. Requirement met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit (first amiodarone outpatient order 5d345f42 authored that day; it is absent from the 2025-09-21 visit list and present from 2025-11-10). Start is on/after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24 (day 14). Requirement met, but that tracing shows QTc ~553 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-02-12 cardiology clinic visit (first order 0d807827 authored that day). Because the start preceded 3/1/2026 the earlier memo's 30-day window is retained, so the ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08 (day 24) - outside 14 days but inside the applicable 30-day window - with sinus rhythm at 68 bpm and QTc ~450 ms. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-04-10 cardiology clinic visit (first order ead8699a authored that day). Start is on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline - so the requirement was not met in time and is now overdue (it would have been met under the superseded 30-day memo). Escitalopram remains current (order b9bce5cd to 2027-01-01).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-08-01 cardiology clinic visit (order 9fa1dfe1, valid to 2026-12-26, and newly listed on that visit's medication list). An ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722) and none is referenced elsewhere, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-08-10 cardiology clinic visit (order d7292a2a), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The 2026-08-25 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG for this patient exists in the chart. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the 2026-09-15 cardiology clinic visit (order 34d26a30, valid to 2027-01-06; first appearance on the medication list). Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due; an ECG should be arranged this month.

At the 2026-09-01 cardiology clinic visit the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the clinic protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, which the 3/1/2026 memo covers, so a follow-up INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the change and no pending outside result is referenced, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 (Condition 66dd1300) during an admission for cerebral infarction. No anticoagulant has ever been ordered: cardiology clinic notes 2025-04-24 through 2026-06-23 list only famotidine, metoprolol and levothyroxine, and the only heparin exposure was a single inpatient prophylaxis dose in 3/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1); guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. Documented thrombocytopenia and history of falling should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current order (authored 2026-08-20, valid to 2027-01-04) and is listed as a current medication at the 2026-08-20 cardiology clinic visit, despite outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The drug was restarted/continued without that review being documented; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was re-issued the same day and the note's own medication list includes both agents. Rivaroxaban must be stopped; combined DOAC therapy carries a major haemorrhage risk in a patient also on clopidogrel.

The 2026-06-10 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', but both ECGs recorded that day contradict it: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.36-0.53 s) with no organised P waves at 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. The documented rhythm and rate are both wrong, and the patient carries an unspecified-atrial-fibrillation diagnosis; rate control and the accuracy of the record need review.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 438668cc, 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26, continuous since 5/2024). Most recent ECG 108018814 (2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~495 ms and Bazett QTc ~529 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L and Mg 1.9 mg/dL on 2026-03-18). Note the 2024-05-14 clinic note characterised this tracing's QT as 'acceptable', which the measured QTc does not support; a repeat ECG is also reasonable given the tracing is nearly three years old.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order e78404bf, 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09). Most recent ECG 106885519 (2025-11-24) is sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a broad low-amplitude T wave, QT ~545 ms and Bazett QTc ~553 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo; QTc rose ~143 ms from the prior tracing (410 ms on 2025-06-07). Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is drug-related. Concurrent warfarin interaction and torsades risk warrant prescriber review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 62da0901, 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; continuous since 10/2023) - a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised where QT prolongation is a concern. Most recent ECG 104821039 (2023-11-10) is sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~480 ms and Bazett QTc ~533 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, and ~147 ms longer than the prior tracing (386 ms, 2020-06-17). Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. Prescriber review of dose/agent and a current ECG are needed.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order c67148bf, 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06; continuous since 2022). Most recent ECG 101515306 (2022-04-27) is sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a very broad T wave, QT ~580 ms and Bazett QTc ~568 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo and ~128 ms longer than the prior tracing (440 ms, 2022-04-06). Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are acceptable though magnesium is at the low end. This 95-year-old is also on warfarin and metoprolol; prescriber review and a repeat ECG are needed.
